correctness.rationale: Three disjoint rail routes force one selected vertex per row in a minimum cut and an internal column attains size three. A gap of at least two columns between adjacent-row selections admits a two-rail detour; differences of at most one give a left/right partition with no surviving crossing edge. Legal slides are one-coordinate unit steps. The coordinatewise meet is feasible; for comparable states, increasing a least current coordinate among those still below target cannot be blocked by a smaller coordinate, since such a tight blocker would itself have to increase for the target to be feasible. Thus paths via the meet attain L1. Each central layer has 12 edges and its next interface 4. In target layer q the worst distance is 2+|i-q|+|j-q|+|k-q|, convex in q, so only the two endpoint layers are needed. The radius lower bound comes from the sum of the endpoint distances and is attained by the stated parity-dependent central states; the two extreme triples attain diameter 3n−5, including n=3. The proof is for all n≥3. Independent bounded check: python /workspace/branches/grid_independent.py, exhaustive two- and three-vertex deletions, original-grid slides and all-pairs Floyd–Warshall for n=3,…,10. Frozen scripts and recorded output were inspected, not executed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact formula for slide displacement on a connected component is inherited. The ≥4-row theorem cannot simply be specialized to three rows; its proof of the separator constraints readily extends to three rows by dropping the extra-row conditions, but neither its slide tables nor the general algorithm establish the resulting all-state geometry.

evidence: Once reachability is known, the three canonical rails and forward-only theorem give L1 immediately. The explicit coordinate constraints are also common to the related cut models where the middle coordinate is internal and there are no extra rows.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The surviving contribution is proving reachability for every feasible pair and deriving the explicit all-state geometry and sharp extremal values, not restating the general shortest-slide result. Jump reachability does not certify slide reachability.

evidence: The exact Resultary match 45171202d901 is the same record. Distinct record 8d1e7a3055c3 has auxiliary terminals adjacent to entire end columns and uses jumps, not slides.
The canonical path description equates slides to adjacent moves on one rail, not jumps.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A minimum s–t vertex cut is a minimum terminal separator. The jump graph has edges joining outer coordinates differing by two within a layer, and the model also allows middle-coordinate end columns. Restricting the common coordinate set and keeping only unit slides gives a different metric problem.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the full quantitative slide geometry of this specific three-rail family. The coordinate constraints overlap strongly with two same-day records, and the Manhattan metric conditional on reachability specializes the general canonical-path theorem. Neither point is a new method. The combination of unrestricted all-pairs reachability and explicit slide order, size, eccentricities, radius and diameter was not covered by the inspected results.
residual_risks: The same-day records have material common structure; no priority order is inferred.
The literature comparison does not exclude unindexed equivalent work or uninspected passages of the 2020 precursor.

Its exact state count and slide geometry distinguish feasibility, travel cost and central configurations under optimum preservation, giving a uniform sharp benchmark rather than a list of verified examples or a general algorithm evaluated at one size.
